title: Observability Lab Standup — dashboard refresh & cost telemetry playtest
content:
Attendees: Priya Nair (chair), Elliot Zhang, Marcus Alvarez, Sara Kim, Tomoko Ito
Date: 2028-01-12 (standup + lab session)
Objective: Quick sync on two parallel experiments: (1) dashboard refresh prototype that surfaces latency x cost heatmaps, and (2) cost-telemetry playtest measuring per-span token cost vs aggregate billing.

Summary of Demos
- Elliot showed the prototype dashboard: combined heatmap where X axis = request percentile (p50,p90,p99), Y axis = model variant, color = estimated cost per 1k requests. Hover provides breakdown: avg tokens, avg KV-cache hit rate, GPU kernel choice. Live demo used a synthetic workload from the stress harness (see linked PR).
- Marcus demoed a lightweight sampling shim for tracer to emit a per-span token_count tag without requiring payload inspection. Implemented as a sidecar filter that reads tokenizer metadata injected earlier in the pipeline. Early perf numbers: ~0.6% added p95 latency at p50 load, ~1.8% at synthetic 2x stress.

Key Observations
- Dashboard UX: product folks liked the side-by-side heatmap + timeline, but asked for a single-click drilldown into the traces that make a cell — action: add trace-link button.
- Cost telemetry: per-span token accounting is feasible with the shim approach but has edge cases for function-calling and streaming responses where tokens are produced in chunks.
- Sampling: uniform 1/20 sampling reduces signal for rare error modes; adaptive sampling based on anomaly score looks promising (sample more when latency spikes or error rates > baseline).

Decisions Taken
- Move forward with a hybrid sampling strategy for the experiment: baseline uniform 1/50 for general traffic + anomaly-triggered full sampling. Rationale: keeps cost low while preserving debug signal during incidents. (Owner: Elliot, JIRA-OBS-358)
- Dashboard 0.1 will ship with heatmap + timeline + trace-link. No alerting in 0.1. (Owner: Priya, JIRA-OBS-342)
- Keep per-span token_count as a non-indexed tag for now to avoid high-cardinality index costs; aggregate rollups will be computed offline and surfaced in the dashboard. (Owner: Marcus)

Open Questions / Risks
- Token attribution accuracy for streaming / function-calling flows — do we attribute partial tokens to intermediate spans? Risk: double-counting leading to misleading cost spikes. Follow-up: design a token attribution protocol that uses monotonic sequence IDs to deduplicate. (Action: Marcus, due 2028-01-19)
- Storage and index cost for per-span fields — even as non-indexed tags, retention of per-span token_count could grow rapidly for high-throughput routes. Need a retention policy and sampled-forwarding pipeline. (Action: Sara to model 90/30/7 retention scenarios)
- Billing mapping: estimated token costs on dashboard must be reconciled with actual billing metrics from finance; tolerance +/- 8% is acceptable initially but confirm. (Action: Priya to sync with finance; linked artifact finance-ticket TBD)

Action Items (short)
- Elliot: Implement anomaly-triggered sampling prototype + unit tests; integrate with sampling-config toggle in feature flag system. (Due: 2028-01-19)
- Marcus: Design token-attribution protocol for streaming and function-calling, write spec and examples. (Due: 2028-01-19)
- Sara: Cost-retention modeling spreadsheet (90/30/7 days) with estimated S3 + index costs; propose retention defaults. (Due: 2028-01-18)
- Priya: Create dashboard 0.1 rollout checklist and stub the trace-link UX flow in the console. (Due: 2028-01-16)
- Tomoko: Run a 24-hour canary with hybrid sampling on staging to capture anomalies. Capture overhead metrics. (Due: 2028-01-15)

Notes from experiment playbook (lab learnings)
- Start small: sampling config should be server-side and feature-flag controlled, not baked in code. This enables fast rollback.
- Aggregate compute: prefer nightly rollups for cost-estimates rather than real-time per-span joins to keep query costs down. Real-time only for high-priority routes.
- Instrumentation: prefer adding lightweight integer tags (token_count) and keep heavy blobs out of spans. Use artifacts for payload-level analysis when necessary (stored off-trace).

Metrics to track during canary
- Tracing overhead: p50/p90/p99 added latency compared to baseline, CPU delta on tracer hosts, memory delta on sidecars.
- Signal quality: percentage of anomalies detected where anomaly-triggered sampling captured full traces. Target >= 90% for critical routes.
- Cost delta: estimated dashboard cost vs actual billing (daily reconciliation), target error < 8%.
- Storage growth: daily increase in span volume and tag cardinality.

Sprint tie-ins
- This work is part of sprint-14 (observability experiments). It blocks the dashboard release sprint item and ties into infra's quantization-cost accounting epic. Please reference sprint board: JIRA sprint-14 (obs).

Reference links / snippets
- PR with sampling shim + tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/712
- Initial dashboard prototype screenshots in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/tools/observability-lab-jan-2028
- Token attribution sketch: see embedded diagram in Marcus' doc (linked in Confluence page)

Retro notes (quick)
- What worked: cross-functional lab-style standup accelerated decisions — keep this cadence weekly for the next 4 weeks.
- What didn't: we underestimated streaming complexity. Need a small spike before wide rollout.

Next meeting
- Quick sync Fri 2028-01-15 post-canary kickoff (15m) + deeper lab review Tue 2028-01-19 (45m).

End of notes.
